roster.name: Michele Bullock
roster.note: Hawkish, data-led. 29 Sep media conference: 'The Board will increase interest rates again if that's what's needed'; unemployment 'a bit tight'; hopes 4.60% is 'restrictive enough'. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-09-29.html

roster.name: Andrew Hauser
roster.note: Most hawkish on the record: inflation the economy's 'one big problem'; rates would rise 'further than otherwise' if expectations slip, 'not at that point yet' (ABC 7.30, 8 Sep 2026). rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-dg-2026-09-08.html

roster.name: Jenny Wilkinson
roster.note: No on-record view on rates in 2026. Placed at the Board's revealed position: the 29 Sep hike was unanimous (9-0). Imputed from the published vote, not the member.

roster.name: Marnie Baker

roster.name: Melinda Cilento
roster.note: Joined 1 Sep 2026 (ex-CEDA CEO). Public comment on productivity and AI, none on rates; voted in the unanimous 29 Sep hike. Placed at the Board's revealed position.

roster.name: Renée Fry-McKibbin

roster.name: Carolyn Hewson
roster.note: Credibility-first: 'inflation expectations are better when anchored. Policy credibility is stronger' (speech, 27 May 2026); no rate call. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-mpb-2026-05-27.html

roster.name: Iain Ross
roster.note: Least hawkish on the record: 'little evidence that a self-sustaining wage-price spiral has emerged'; labour market easing towards balance (speech, 22 Sep 2026). Still voted for the 29 Sep hike. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-mpb-2026-09-22.html

kill_criteria.label: 3-month BBSW/cash spread blows out
kill_criteria.note: Bank funding stress. Widens the wedge between what you are trading and the policy rate you have a view on.

kill_criteria.label: Cash rate trades away from target
kill_criteria.note: AONIA normally sits on the target under ample reserves. A persistent gap means IB is settling on something other than the rate you are forecasting.

kill_criteria.label: 3-month BBSW moves more than 25bp in a fortnight
kill_criteria.note: The short end has repriced without you. Whatever your q was, it was set against a different curve.

kill_criteria.label: Trimmed mean CPI surprises by more than 0.3pp
kill_criteria.note: The RBA targets the trimmed mean. Quarterly, so this fires rarely and hard.

kill_criteria.label: Unemployment rate moves 0.3pp from the RBA's forecast
kill_criteria.note: Full employment is half the mandate. Set against the latest SMP forecast, not the last print.

kill_criteria.label: AUD/USD moves more than 5% in a month
kill_criteria.note: A big currency move does the RBA's work for it, or undoes it. Matters more here than for a closed economy.

kill_criteria.label: Governor or Deputy signals a change of stance
kill_criteria.note: Only two voices reliably move the curve. Outside the blackout, a speech can reprice the meeting on its own.
